```json
{"id": "mabkhara-smoke-thread", "verdict": "rewrite", "score": 3, "styleFit": 4, "literal": true, "problems": ["The ember sitting in a flared bowl line with smoke rising is a small picture of the incense burner, not an abstraction of it.", "The brass stud row reads as a decorative border pasted on top. It is not part of the composition.", "The gulf-arabic-first tag is not earned: no real craft grammar from the mabkhara's making, only its silhouette and studs.", "The smoke thread is a single wobbly line with little depth, so it looks thin rather than crafted at 320 by 180."]
, "fix": "Remove the bowl line and the ember-as-object. Keep one low warm bloom as the only light and turn the smoke into a slow, faint field of fine curling lines that drift upward and dissolve before the text zone. Move the stud rhythm into a quiet dot-grid texture taken from the burner's pierced brass pattern, with one slow glint. Aim for dark-luminous, with the brass texture as the second voice."}
```

```json
{"id": "talli-silver-line-draw", "verdict": "rewrite", "score": 3, "styleFit": 3, "literal": false, "problems": ["A center-out underline draw is the stock tab indicator move. Nothing in the timing carries the braid, so the Talli source barely shows.", "Redrawing from the center on every change ignores where the selection came from, which makes it feel decorative rather than spatial.", "scaleY(1.6) on a hairline will render blurry at subpixel thickness and reads as a wobble more than a settle.", "The brightness glint at full width is fine, but it holds too long, from offset 0 to 0.6, to feel like a brief catch of light."]}
```

**fix:** Borrow the over-under rhythm of the braid instead of a plain wipe. Have two half strands enter from the left and right edges of the tab and cross past the center by a few pixels before settling, using a quick cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) over about 280ms. Keep the line at fixed hairline thickness with no scaleY. Limit the silver glint to a short brightness peak around offset 0.4. When the previous tab is known, slide the line from it so the move stays spatial, calm and crisp, in keeping with gulf-arabic-first restraint.

```json
{"id": "qatt-figure-row-count", "verdict": "rewrite", "score": 2, "styleFit": 2, "literal": false, "problems": ["A 90 ms stagger inside a 2400 ms alternate loop makes all rows rise and fall almost together, so it reads as a generic skeleton pulse, not an even count.", "The symmetric ease-in-out breathing has no stepped rhythm, so the even repeat borrowed from Al Qatt Al Asiri figures is lost.", "The 2px lift with scaleY 0.9 is too faint to read as figures settling onto a shared baseline.", "There is no right-to-left order or other Gulf grammar, so the gulf-arabic-first tag is not earned."]
, "fix": "Make it a discrete count: fill each child in turn, right to left, at a fixed 140 ms step with a short crisp rise (about 260 ms, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)). Hold all rows lit briefly, then reset them together, with no alternate direction, so the loop reads as one calm, even tally."}
```

```json
{"id": "bracket-clamp-grid", "verdict": "rewrite", "score": 3, "styleFit": 4, "literal": true, "problems": ["It draws two literal square bracket glyphs as the subject, which counts as letter-like glyphs.", "The amber glint reads as a small glow, which drifts off a no-glow matte style.", "The baseline grid is so faint in the header band that the texture voice barely registers.", "The brackets clamp an empty center, and nothing tells you what is being selected or held."]}
```

The verdict needs a fix line, so here it is.

**Fix:** Keep the clamping rhythm, but drop the bracket hooks. Make the center area a single tone step lighter than the #121417 ground, bounded only by two hairline vertical edges in #6b717a that ease in by a few pixels and settle on a custom curve. Replace the glint with a flat 1 px amber tick that steps along one edge, and make the 8 px baseline grid slightly more legible. The aim is pure dark-quiet-matte tone steps and hairlines.

```json
{"id": "block-layer-press-line", "verdict": "rewrite", "score": 3, "styleFit": 3, "literal": false, "problems": ["The three press lines are not visible, so the layer-by-layer printing reads as one static grid of diamonds with no process behind it.", "The off-register offset and the separate colour layers are lost at this size; the red and ochre become scattered specks that muddy the tan outlines.", "The band runs hard into the left edge and stops abruptly on the right, so it looks cropped rather than like a printed length running into bare cloth.", "Motion across the frames is barely detectable, and the straight square grid feels like a generic glyph texture rather than the even half-drop rhythm of block print."]
, "fix": "Keep the stamping process, but make each press station legible: draw a faint hairline at each station and step the layers clearly (outline in ink, then accent fill, then support gap dots). Offset each layer by a visible 1 to 2 px with a slight ink-spread grain. Use a half-drop grid with gaps as wide as the stamps, and fade the band into the cloth at both ends so it sits as one quiet textured strip under a progress label."}
```

```json
{"id": "memphis-dot-grid-ring", "verdict": "rewrite", "score": 3, "styleFit": 3, "literal": false, "problems": ["The corner cluster of dot grid, outlined pink ring and teal arc reads like a stock Memphis template sticker, not a borrowed rule.", "The bottom left terrazzo flecks are so faint and scattered that they read as dust or render noise, not intent.", "It ignores the lens's real grammar: the one shape per palm of spacing and the even beat of stripes and squiggles along a straight edge.", "Three different motifs packed into one corner make it busier than flat-color-field's 2 or 3 flat colours and one strong mark."]}
```

Fix: Keep the calm paper ground and the pop-then-rest timing. Build the piece from the lens's rhythm rather than a sticker cluster:

- Run one flat stripe or squiggle band at an even beat along a single straight edge.
- Snap the dot grid to a real layout grid.
- Place at most two flat confetti shapes, about a palm apart, in the accent colours.
- Drop the faint flecks.
- Use a crisp stepped ease on the pop-in so it reads as flat-color-field with a playful accent.

```json
{"id": "alula-strata-drift", "verdict": "rewrite", "score": 3, "styleFit": 2, "literal": false, "problems": ["The boundaries are smooth sine-like waves, so it reads as generic wavy layer wallpaper or dunes, not stacked rock strata.", "The palette is muddy brown on brown with low contrast: the lit lips and the sun sweep barely register, and the #b5532a accent never shows as a focal point.", "It is a soft digital gradient render with no hand, print or grain voice, so it misses the illustrative-handmade tag.", "The band thicknesses are nearly even, which loses the irregular rhythm that makes strata feel real."],
"fix": "Keep the strata grammar but make the bands near-horizontal with irregular, stepped thicknesses and only a slight slow drift. Give each band a crisp one-weight hairline lip in the ink colour, add a fine printed grain or striation texture as the second voice, and let one band carry the terracotta accent so the hard sun angle has a clear focus. Keep the calm dark space above for text."}
```
